messages:
lia (partnerships): Partner 'HelixAI' is moving to a hybrid model: they report GPU-seconds from on-device inference and want marketplace to bill customers in vCPU-seconds for invoicing parity with our Dedicated offering. They want us to accept both event types and map them into a single entitlement. Need input on normalization, currency/region differences, and contract implications.

igor (eng-platform): interesting. two immediate choices: normalize at ingest (convert gpu_seconds -> vcpu_seconds using partner-provided conversion ratio) or store both and let billing decide. Normalizing early simplifies downstream but hides original telemetry.

mona (billing): we prefer canonical units for invoicing. But conversion ratio must be auditable and deterministic. Also, GPU capacity and vCPU are not 1:1 across regions and instance types; a static ratio may be disputed. Suggest partner includes metadata: model_type, gpu_type, and conversion_ratio_signed (HMAC) they agree to.

eli (finance): flags: currency conversion + regional price differences. If Helix reports usage in eu-west and we bill in USD, FX rates matter for historical backfills. Also revenue recognition may change if we convert units post-facto. We need conversion rules stored with timestamp and approver.

jules (legal): contract side: ask partner to sign off on the conversion ratios and a small tolerance for measurement variance. Also include an audit clause allowing us to request raw telemetry if disputes > threshold.

igor (eng-platform): implementation sketch:
- Ingest accepts two payload flavors: {"unit":"gpu_seconds", "gpu_type":"A100", "units":1234, "event_id":"...", "conversion_ratio":"r=3.2;sig=..."} OR {"unit":"vcpu_seconds", "units":3950, ...}.
- If gpu_seconds and valid signed conversion_ratio present, compute canonical_vcpu = units * ratio and store both raw_units and canonical_vcpu plus ratio_meta.
- If gpu_seconds without signed ratio, store raw and route to manual mapping queue.
- All conversions produce ledger entries referencing ratio_id and sign-off metadata.

mona (billing): we also need idempotency and dedupe. For hybrid setups the same work might be reported twice (device and marketplace). Dedupe key suggestion: H(event_id || partner_id || canonical_bucket). If both gpu and vcpu arrive for same event, prefer partner-signed vcpu (explicit billing unit) over derived canonical_vcpu.

lia (partnerships): partner is OK providing signed ratios per-model and per-region. They asked whether we can accept a small per-event tolerance (e.g., +/-2%) so minor measurement jitter doesn't trigger disputes.

eli (finance): tolerance OK but must be part of the run metadata. For any adjustment outside tolerance finance approval required. Also FX: store the FX rate used for conversion on the ledger (timestamped).

jules (legal): also include an SLA for changing ratios: partners must give 30 days notice before changing conversion metadata. Changes before that window are not retroactive unless mutually agreed.

igor (eng-platform): sample ingest payload we'll accept:
```
POST /marketplace/usage
{
  "partner_id":"helixai",
  "entitlement_id":"ent-helix-01",
  "event_id":"evt-20260401-0001",
  "window_start":"2026-04-01T12:00:00Z",
  "units": 1200,
  "unit":"gpu_seconds",
  "gpu_type":"a100-80gb",
  "conversion_ratio_signed":"r=3.25;ratio_id=ratio-202603;sig=base64...",
  "region":"eu-west-1"
}
```
On ingest: verify signature, compute canonical_vcpu=1200*3.25 -> store raw + canonical, write ledger row with ratio_id, fx_rate, and approver metadata.

mona (billing): operational rules: prefer explicit vcpu events; if canonical_vcpu and explicit vcpu both exist for same ent+bkt, do a reconciliation pass and, by default, trust explicit vcpu. Emit a reconciliation report weekly for partners in hybrid mode.

ops-bot: job "hybrid-normalize-sim" queued: sample run will process 50k events in staging.

lia (partnerships): partner requests a one-time backfill converting last 3 months of gpu_seconds to vcpu_seconds using current signed ratios. They also want an export of per-account diffs before we touch ledger rows.

eli (finance): backfill caution: post-conversion invoices may change revenue recognition. Any backfill that changes >$1k per account requires finance approval and runbook. We'll require a dry-run export and signed change request from partner.

jules (legal): add a clause that backfills require an explicit partner-signed request and Redwood reserves right to decline if it materially affects billing. Also require indemnity for measurement errors.

igor (eng-platform): next steps: 1) implement signed-ratio verification + canonical store (spike this week) 2) billing to draft reconciliation logic and weekly report format (mona) 3) finance/legal to define approval thresholds and backfill policy (eli/jules) 4) partnerships to collect partner ratio manifests and schedule staging run (lia). ETA: staging sim in 7 days.

lia (partnerships): thanks all 1. I'll schedule the partner call and share the staging run link. Tagging @igor @mona @eli @jules. :white_check_mark:
